spanish_col.subtitle: (López Austin & García Quintana 2000)
spanish_col.markdown:
herido. Y si alguno que era bien dispuesto enfermaba en estos días, decían que las diosas le habían deseado la hermosura y se la habían quitado. A los que nacían en este signo, varones, decían que serían bien acondicionados y regocijados, y amigos de todos. Y que serían cantores o bailadores o pintores, o deprenderían algún buen oficio por haber nacido en tal signo.

La segunda casa deste signo se llamaba _ume malinalli_. Era mal afortunada. Los que nacían en este signo engendraban muchos hijos, en ninguno dellos se lograba. Todos se murían ante tiempo.

La tercera casa deste signo se llamaba _ei ácatl_; la cuarta, _nahui océlotl_; la quinta, _macuilli cuauhtli_; la sexta, _chicuace cozcacuauhtli_; la séptima, _chicome olin_; la octava, _chicuei técpatl_; la nona, _chicunahui quiáhuitl_; la décima, _matlactli xúchitl_; la undécima, _matlactlioce cipactli_; la dudodécima, _matlactliomome écatl_; la terciadécima, _matlactliomei calli_.
 
Todas las otras casas deste signo tienen las condiciones de los números en que cayen, como ya está dicho arriba; que las terceras casas son buenas; las cuartas y quintas y sextas, malas; y las séptimas, buenas; y las octavas y nonas, malas; y las décimas y undécimas y terciadécimas, buenas.

spanish_col.subtitle: (García Garagarza 2023)
spanish_col.markdown:
afflicted him or her. And if someone who had a good disposition fell ill during those days, they said that the goddesses had coveted his or her beauty and had taken it away from this person. They said that the males born under this sign would be good-natured, joyful, and friends with everyone, and that they would become singers, dancers, painters, or would learn a good trade, since they were born under that sign.

The second house of this sign was called Ome Malinalli, and it was unlucky. Those born under this sign would bear many children, but none of them would survive. They would all die before their time.

The third house of this sign was called Yei Acatl; the fourth, Nahui Ocelotl; the fifth, Macuilli Cuauhtli; the sixth, Chicuace Cozcacuauhtli; the seventh, Chicome Ollin; the eighth, Chicuei Tecpatl; the ninth, Chiucnahui Quiahuitl; the tenth, Mahtlactli Xochitl; the eleventh, Matlactlionce Cipactli; the twelfth, Mahtlactli omome Ehecatl; the thirteenth, Mahtlactli omey Calli.

All of the other houses of this sign have the qualities of the numbers on which they fall, as has already been mentioned above: so the third houses are good; the fourth, fifth, and sixth are bad; the seventh are good; the eighth and ninth are bad; and the tenth, eleventh, twelfth, and thirteenth are good.

nahuatl_col.subtitle: (Anderson & Dibble 1953–1982)
nahuatl_col.markdown:
[in]tla aca ipan opeuh mococoa, qujteilhujaia in titici, ca tlanauiz, aocmo qujçaz, ca omotenamjcti, ipan oqujzque in cioapipilti, ca intemoian, imêcoian in opeuh, ca oeleujloc: 

auh no ioan mjtoa, intla aca qualli yiollo, in qualli itonal, ioan qualli itlachieliz: vncan qujtlacalhujaia, qujtoaia: ca çan oqueleujque, oqujnmonamjcti in cioapipilti. 

Auh in aqujn ipan tlacatia, ie qujqualittaia, qujtoaia: intla oqujchtli ipan otlacat, ca moteaaujltiliz, motececemeltiliz, acan tlaelittoz, muchi tlacatl icnjuh iez, ioan aço cujcanj, mjtotianj, anoço tlacujlo, itla ic totoltecatiz ipampa ca njman iuhquj, in jtonal ce oçomatli, iuh qujtoa: çan ie much iuhquj, in jzqujtetl oçomatli in ie mjieccan omjto, in quenamj innemac, ipan tlacati. 

Auh in vme malinalli: njman amo qualli, qujtoa tequanj: in aqujn vncã tlacati, cenca vel mopilhoatia, iuhqujn tetl icaque, iuhqujn mjchaiatza ipilhoan, çan iê amo ce moquetza, çan much vnmjctiuj. Etª. (in iuh omjto). 

Auh in ei acatl, ioan nauj ocelutl macujlli quauhtli, chiquacen cozcaquauhtli, chicome olin chicuei tecpatl, chicunavi qujaujtl, matlactli suchitl, matlactloce cipactli, matlactlomome hecatl, matlactli vmei calli: in jxqujch in cencalpan tonalli, çan ie much iuhquj

nahuatl_col.subtitle: (Anderson & Dibble 1953–1982)
nahuatl_col.markdown:
if someone began to sicken, the physicians told him that he would become dangerously sick; he would not recover. For he had come upon the Princesses, and they had set upon him; it was the time of their descent and arrival when [this sickness] began. For it was [so] willed.

And likewise it was said that if someone were of good standing, of a good day sign, and able, if at this time they injured him, they said that the Princesses had indeed willed it upon him and that he had contended with them.[^1]

And he who was then born they regarded favorably. They said that if it were a man who was then born, he would entertain others and give them solace. Nowhere would he be hated; everyone would be his friend. And [he would be], perchance, a singer, a dancer, or a scribe; he would produce some work of art. For such, then, was his day sign, One Monkey. So they said that indeed thus it came to pass on each of the different Monkey [day signs], as hath been told in many places of the gifts of those then born.

And Two Grass was in no way good. They said it was a wild beast. He who was then born would beget very many sons; they would stand like stones; like spawned fish would his sons be. Nevertheless not one would grow, but all merely died, etc. (So hath it been told.)
